column1: # ci/fork-upstreams.tsv -- the real upstream of each idesign0 fork submodule.
#   update_forked_submodules.sh only touches a submodule that has an `upstream` git
#   remote. That remote lives in .git/modules/<path>/config, which is NEVER committed,
#   so it exists only on a developer machine. In CI every submodule is a fresh clone
#   with just `origin`, which is why the updater reported "Skipped (648) -- no upstream
#   remote" on every run and had never updated anything there.
#   sync-submodules-branches.sh cannot help: it reads the candidate upstream URL from
#   .gitmodules, which is the very URL git cloned `origin` from, so its
#   This file is the missing record. scripts/add_upstream_remotes.sh reads it and adds
#   the remote, so the updater can work off a checkout it did not create.
#   Generated from `gh api repos/idesign0/<repo> --jq .parent.clone_url`, i.e. GitHub's
#   own record of what each fork was forked from. Not guessed from the name.
# Entries listed in ci/fork-no-autoupdate.txt are skipped regardless of what is here.
# NOT RECORDED -- GitHub reports no parent for these (created with
# `gh repo create` + push rather than forked), so the true upstream is not
# discoverable. Left out deliberately: the updater skips them exactly as it
# does today. Add a line by hand only if you are certain of the upstream.
# Recovered by hand: GitHub reports no parent for these forks (created with
# `gh repo create` + push), so the upstream was confirmed by finding a commit
# shared between our branch and the candidate upstream, not by guessing names.
# verified: shares commit 1489fc93 with ros2/cartographer on branch ros2
# verified: shares commit f8b2cca2 with ros2/rmw on branch kilted
